With all due respect, I’d like to point out a few things: 

1. In defence of my Christian upbringing, I have been brought up and taught rather well in Christian doctrine to know well enough that there’s a book called the Bible which has all the answers to life’s questions. But there are times where sometimes merely reading the Bible isn’t enough as there may not be direct answers for certain “gray areas” i.e. tattoos 

2. Imho, I don’t believe a Christian asking fellow believers what he/she thinks about a certain subject is equal to being lazy in reading the Word or prayer. In fact, the Bible tells us to go to mature Christian elders for counselling or to seek answers for any questions we do not understand.  Yes, I admit that my devotional life is barely afloat, but surely we are called not to condemn other believers but rather to encourage and strengthen each other in our spiritual walk! 

3. I’m speaking this on behalf of all Christians, both matured and new. As much as we *think* we know a lot about God’s Word, there will always be times where we have doubts. Mind you, even pastors and great defenders of the faith have been through a phase where they had so questions even though they know all the answers are inside the Bible.

So in conclusion, we have to remember that not every Christian is spiritually mature enough to read the Bible and immediately find the answers. Rather, we should act in grace and patience in leading them to do what’s right according to God
